messages:
olivia: Heads-up — since 10:03 we started seeing intermittent SCIM provisioning 403s for a subset of customers after their IdP pushed a JWKS rotation. Logs show token signature verify failures.

kyle: can you paste an example error?

olivia: sure — from prod-ingest: `2026-03-23T10:03:21Z ERROR scim: token verify failed: token.signature: invalid (kid not found) user=acct-123)`. Also noticed egress to idp jwks_uri is 200 but payload contains the new kid only.

mira: are we caching JWKS? we have a 5m cache on jwks fetch in the library. if idp rotates without overlap we can get hit.

samir: yes client caches. most IdPs publish old+new for a while, but looks like this vendor did atomic rotate (new set only). That matches `kid not found`.

olivia: affected flows: SCIM provisioning (onboarding) and any token-based RBAC change webhook. Audit logs show a handful of `rbac:change attempt denied 403` entries that line up with the failures.

alex: quick mitigation: fallback to re-fetching jwks on signature failure and allow a short retry window. but we need to be careful with rate limits to idp.

mira: Agreed — implement immediate re-fetch if `kid` missing and only for tokens with `alg` we support. Also add a single TTL-bypass for the cache for 15s after a re-fetch to pick up a rotation.

sre-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — #inc-2026-041-jwks-rotation — severity: P2 — owners: @kyle @samir — runbook: identity/jwks-rotation.md

kyle: I'm taking ownership. immediate next steps: 1) enable aggressive re-fetch on signature-miss (hotfix), 2) add alert for spike of `kid not found`, 3) contact the IdP and ask for rotation timeline and whether they can publish old keys for a rollover period.

samir: for hotfix, patch snippet below (python pseudo):
```python
try:
  verify(token)
except KidNotFound:
  jwks_client.force_refresh()  # bypass cache once
  verify(token)
```
This avoids wider TTL changes.

olivia: +1. also we should map the failed token IDs to affected audit entries so we can surface to customers and to security for the RBAC-change denials. I'll export matches from logs.

alex: question re: KMS — are any of these tokens JWE-encrypted with KMS-wrapped content? i.e., could KMS rotation be related?

mira: no, these are standard signed JWTs from IdP (RS256). KMS used for storing our signing keys for service-to-service tokens is unrelated. But we should double-check audit trails in KMS for coincident rotations — low probability.

kyle: FYI I notified the IdP SRE. Their reply: they rotated without old keys due to a bug in their deploy tooling. they're rolling back a change and will publish old+new within 10m.

olivia: timeline: 10:03 first errors, 10:07 spike to 120/minute, 10:12 we applied hotfix (force-refresh on miss), 10:15 errors dropped. I'll attach logs and counts to the incident.

samir: follow-ups: 1) add telemetry: histogram of `kid_not_found` by vendor/tenant, 2) make `kid_not_found` create a trace/span for easier debug, 3) update onboarding docs to encourage vendors to provide key overlap window, 4) run an internal test to simulate atomic JWKS replace.

mira: RBAC audit: we should mark the 403s as "authorization failure due to identity provider validation" in our audit UI so compliance teams can distinguish from policy denials. that helps customers and security.

alex: agree — add a new audit code `IDP_JWKS_KID_MISSING` and wire it to the affected entries. also file a vuln/ops note: if IdP fails to publish overlap it creates a transient DoS on auth flows. classify as operational risk and document mitigations.

kyle: postmortem plan: short incident note (P2), timeline, root cause (IdP atomic JWKS replace), mitigation (client-side force-refresh on missing kid + alerting), long-term (backoff-safe cache TTL window, vendor onboarding checks, automated JWKS-fetch test in CI).

olivia: I've created the postmortem draft in the incident doc and added the log exports. dropping a snippet of the failing auth header to help security triage:
```
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsImtpZCI6Im5ld19raWQiLCJ0eXAiOiJKV1QifQ....
```

samir: I'll open a PR for the hotfix. please review quickly. target deploy to canary then global. we should also add a unit/integration test that simulates rotate-without-overlap.

mira: can we also add a guard in the token parser so that if the `kid` is missing entirely we fail fast with a specific audit message? fewer ambiguous failures = easier compliance reports.

kyle: yes, add `if not token.kid: audit('MISSING_KID'); reject` — that's separate from missing kid in JWKS.

olivia: thanks all. keeping incident open until IdP confirms they restored old keys and we see zero errors for 30m. will post updates. :thumbsup:
